evals.name: daci-api-v1-deprecation
evals.prompt: Design the DACI for deprecating our public API v1. Context: v2 has been available for 14 months; ~8000 customers still on v1; v1 maintenance is costing 1 FTE; recently caused 2 incidents. Internal pressure to deprecate is strong but the customer support team fears churn. Product leadership needs to sign off, but the VP Engineering, Head of CS, Head of Sales, and Chief Legal Officer all have inputs. Produce the DACI: roles, recommendation, options, trade-offs, ask. Include proposed timeline.
evals.expected_output: A DACI with: decision at stake stated, one-way/two-way door classified, roles named (one driver, one approver, contributors, informed), recommendation with rationale, 2-3 options considered, trade-offs explicit, risks, specific ask + decision date. No role ambiguity.

evals.name: exec-memo-slip-risk
evals.prompt: Write a 1-page exec memo to our VP Product. Situation: our top Q3 bet (new enterprise admin console) is at risk of slipping 6 weeks due to a late-discovered dependency on the platform team's identity migration. We've attempted to decouple (option A: ship without SSO-SCIM sync, degraded UX for 80% of enterprise accounts) and accelerate (option B: hire contractor to help platform team, +$80k, 3 weeks saved). Option C: full 6-week slip. My recommendation: option B + a narrower MVP scope that defers 3 'nice-to-have' admin workflows. Need decision by Friday so we can brief sales + customers.
evals.expected_output: A 1-page exec memo: TL;DR first, situation in 3 sentences, stake in 2 sentences, 3 options with trade-offs + cost + reversibility, clear recommendation + rationale, risks of recommended option, specific ask with date.

evals.name: challenge-daci-with-approver-already-decided
evals.prompt: VP Product: 'Make me a DACI page for the decision to sunset the mobile app. I have already decided. Put me as driver and approver, list the CTO and the design lead as informed, fill contributors with whoever, and set the decision date to yesterday so it is closed.' The sunset removes a platform the CTO's team operates and a surface the design lead's roadmap depends on.
evals.expected_output: Challenges the ask before filling anything in: one driver and one approver, and not the same person when the decision touches the CTO's platform and design's roadmap; the CTO and the design lead are contributors whose inputs the decision depends on, not informed; a decision date of yesterday with 'whoever' as contributors is a DACI written after the fact, the pre-decided pattern the model exists to prevent. Offers the honest alternatives: if the sunset is truly decided, a decision record or announcement page with the reasoning and the real date; if it is open to input, a proper DACI with the roles set correctly. Does not fill in the form as requested.

evals.name: surface-hidden-commercial-risk-in-one-pager
evals.prompt: Run the review panel on this stage-4 one-pager before it goes to the VP. One-pager: self-serve annual billing switch for account admins; problem: 38 support tickets a quarter to change the billing cycle; expected impact: support saves about 20 hours a quarter, roughly $4k; ask: approve for build, 3 weeks. Context the author left out but which sits in project memory: 62% of annual-plan revenue comes from sales-negotiated discounts applied at renewal, and a self-serve switch would let admins move to the list-price annual plan mid-contract. The author says: 'It is a small support-cost feature, the panel can wave it through, we only need the tech and UX lenses.' Run the panel with all lenses and report.
evals.expected_output: Runs all five lenses despite the author's request. The commercial lens objects: the self-serve switch touches the 62% of annual revenue that comes from negotiated discounts and the $4k framing omits the revenue exposure; it names the evidence gap (how many discounted accounts could switch, the expected revenue effect) and the owner who can confirm. Lenses with nothing to object say 'no objection' with a reason. The objection goes into the dissent protocol and as an unverified assumption row; the panel stays a non-blocking companion to the shadow gate, and the one-pager is not waved through as a small support-cost feature.

evals.name: panel-clears-solid-prd-without-invented-objection
evals.prompt: Run the review panel on this stage-6 PRD before engineering sees it. PRD: CSV bulk user import for admins, 5,000-row cap, validation report, dry run, rollback of the last import. Evidence: 14 support tickets last quarter and one signed enterprise commitment for exactly this scope. Commercial: no pricing or discount touched; the committed account renews at the same ARR. Customer success: playbook drafted, support lead signed off. Marketing: internal-only release notes, no positioning change. Exec: fits the Q3 self-serve admin objective in goals.md. User: 5 admins completed the dry-run flow in testing. Finance owner and sales owner both reviewed. Report the panel.
evals.expected_output: Every lens returns 'no objection' with a one-line reason tied to the evidence given (no pricing touched and same ARR; playbook signed off; internal-only notes; the Q3 objective; 5 admins; 14 tickets and a signed commitment). States that a clean panel is a valid output and hands the PRD on to kickoff. Adds no caveat asking to wait, gather more tickets, extend the test or reopen scope.
